top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye. The magic-wavelength lattice, with the light shift cancelled while many neutral atoms sit in the Lamb-Dicke regime, is a distinct mechanism from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. The 1e-18 performance has been reproduced and cross-checked by independent laboratories on different species, which is the kind of quantitative verification I weigh most. It already yields physical results such as millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and bounds on drifting constants. The citation should name invention and realisation together. Ye was not a 2005 laureate, as the round-2 exchange corrected, so there is no repeat-laureate objection. The costs are the omission of Lemonde, Ludlow, Oates, Takamoto and others, and priority dates I cannot check myself, but the evidence heard supports the two-name credit. No award is clearly worse than a mature, verified achievement with a defensible allocation.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to Katori, Ye or any lattice-clock group
